sentences.text: Pliolymbus is an extinct genus of grebe found in the United States and Mexico.
This genus contains only one known species, P. baryosteus.
The animal possessed a skeleton that was far more robust than those of living grebes.
Scientists have recovered a total of six specimens of this creature.
Specimens of Pliolymbus were collected in Kansas in the summer of 1950 by Claude W. Hibbard.
The species Pliolymbus baryosteus was named in 1967 by Bertram G. Murray.
A specimen from Lake Chapala was published by Howard in 1969, having been collected during surveys in 1926, 1958, and 1963.
Pliolymbus is classified within the family Podicipedidae.
Pliolymbus belongs to an extinct lineage of grebes with no close living relatives, dying out by the end of the Pliocene.
Pliolymbus lived from the Piacenzian age of the Pliocene to the Gelasian age of the Pleistocene.
The time range for Pliolymbus is estimated from 2.58 to 0.0117 million years ago.
Fossils of Pliolymbus have been found in the Rexroad Formation in Kansas and at Lake Chapala in Jalisco.
Olson (1985) questioned the validity of the genus Pliolymbus, suggesting P. baryosteus might actually be a species of Podiceps.
